newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone rebels say they have sacked leader.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebels say they have sacked leader.

text.p: A senior member of Sierra Leone's rebel Revolutionary United Front (RUF) said on Saturday that the high command had sacked its leader Foday Sankoh for blocking a deal to end almost six years of civil war.

Captain Philip Palmer, military representative on the RUF's external delegation, told Reuters that the decision was unanimous and was taken on Friday night after intensive radio contacts with rebel commanders and others in Sierra Leone.
Palmer, a founder member of the RUF, confirmed a report from the Nigeriaian ambassador in Sierra Leone that Sankoh was effectively under house arrest in Nigeria's commercial capital Lagos.

"With a view to promoting the spirit of healing and reconciliation and a rapid return to normalcy in Sierra Leone, the RUF High Command declares with immediate effect, the leadership role of corporal Foday Sankoh terminated," Palmer, 39, said in a written statement dated Saturday.
"For now we are trying to restructure the leadership to fill the vacuum," he told Reuters by telephone from the Ivorian town of Danane, near the border with Guinea and Liberia.
Sierra Leone, rich in diamonds and other minerals, is one of the world's poorest nations.

Sankoh, who took up arms in 1991, signed a peace deal with President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah in Ivory Coast on November 30. Implementation has dragged, suggesting that the deal was unravelling. Each side accuses the other of truce violations.

Palmer's statement, delivered to Reuter's office in Ivory Coast, denounced what it called Sankoh's "unyielding determination to thwart the peace process and prolong the suffering of the people of Sierra Leone".

The statement said that Sankoh, who had spent most of the past year in Ivory Coast, persistently refused to meet U.N. officials and members of a peace commission who travelled to Abidjan to discuss the implementation process with him.
It also accused him of refusing to nominate members to joint monitoring and demobilising committees.
Officials in Ivory Coast say Sankoh went to Nigeria on a private visit without informing his Ivorian hosts. Nigerian officials say he arrived there on March 2.

Nigeria's ambassador to Freetown, Alhaji Mohamed Abubakar, told Reuters on Wednesday that Sankoh was detained and questioned at Lagos airport after turning up there on a private visit with a pistol and ammunition. "He was taken to Lagos where is is now under house arrest," the ambassador said.
Tejan Kabbah took office a year ago after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule.
His government ordered the army and its Kamajor traditional hunter allies on March 6 to flush out what it called rebel raiders, accusing RUF fighters of killing civilians and ambushing vehicles.
At the time, Deputy Defence Minister Samuel Hinga Norman accused Sankoh of trying to wreck the peace deal.
Nigeria, the regional power in West Africa, has a battalion of troops in Sierra Leone. They helped to protect installations in the capital Freetown during the war.
The two countries, both former British colonies, signed a new military training cooperation agreement on March 7.
The war has killed more than 10,000 people.
